replies.body:
@lmolkova I agree that a compaction block should be modeled as a message part when it is present in provider input/output. The block is part of the conversation state, its order is semantically important, and for providers like Anthropic it must be passed back on later turns to preserve the compacted history. A boolean alone cannot express whether the block was emitted, where it appeared, what summary/content it carried, or whether later requests preserved it.

However  the boolean is also useful for token accounting. Once a conversation is compacted, subsequent inference spans may show a much lower `gen_ai.usage.input_tokens` count because the effective model input is now a compacted representation rather than the full prior conversation. 
`gen_ai.conversation.compacted=true` lets operators distinguish a real workload-size change from a context-management event. It also makes before/after analysis straightforward: filter by `gen_ai.conversation.id`, find the spans before and after the first compacted turn, and compare token usage around that transition.

So I would model this as both:
- a `compaction` message part in `gen_ai.output.messages` when the provider emits one, and in `gen_ai.input.messages` when the client passes one back;
- `gen_ai.conversation.compacted=true` on the inference span when the effective input/output for that call involved compaction.

I believe if we only add the message part, users can reconstruct the boolean in ideal traces, but may miss it if they're not recording messages due to PII concerns. On the other hand, upon deeper reflection, if we only add the boolean, users lose the correctness/debugging view of whether the compacted state was preserved. Hence, I'm thinking of adding `CompactionPart` as:

```
  CompactionPart:
    type: object
    additionalProperties: true
    properties:
      type:
        const: compaction
      content:
        type: string
        description: The unencrypted compacted conversation summary, when available.
      id:
        type: string
        description: Provider-assigned identifier for the compaction item/block, when available.
    required:
      - type
```

Lmk your thoughts.

+            text = block.get("text") if isinstance(block, dict) else getattr(block, "text", None)

replies.body: @trask I am under the assumption that`gen_ai.conversation.compacted` will be emitted only when compaction is known to have occurred. If instrumentation does not know, or no compaction signal is exposed by the provider/framework, we should leave the attribute unset rather than emit false. This is because imo emitting false can be misleading because absence of an observed compaction event is not the same as knowing compaction did not happen, especially for provider-side behavior(please note only anthropic and openai are doing server side compaction currently). So the useful states are: unset = unknown/not reported, true = compaction occurred. But lmk if you think we can do it differently I am open to changing this.

> absence of an observed compaction event is not the same as knowing compaction did not happen

what if you _know_ that compaction hasn't occurred? should you set it to `false` or leave it blank?
I'm leaning towards leaving it blank.

I don't think we have precedent for this.

Here's the closest that we have:

`gen_ai.request.stream`

> [If unset, the request is assumed to be non-streaming.](model/gen-ai/spans.yaml#L184-L186)

`messaging.destination.temporary`

> [When missing, the value is assumed to be `false`.](https://github.com/open-telemetry/semantic-conventions/blob/085cf2230203d9fb552edf94e035ee9da64ec39d/model/messaging/spans.yaml#L53-L55)

`messaging.destination.anonymous`

> [When missing, the value is assumed to be `false`.](https://github.com/open-telemetry/semantic-conventions/blob/085cf2230203d9fb552edf94e035ee9da64ec39d/model/messaging/spans.yaml#L56-L58)

`messaging.kafka.message.tombstone`

> [When missing, the value is assumed to be `false`.](https://github.com/open-telemetry/semantic-conventions/blob/085cf2230203d9fb552edf94e035ee9da64ec39d/model/messaging/spans.yaml#L160-L162)

Would this work?

Otherwise, we could consider something like this:

```suggestion
      This attribute is a positive indicator of context compaction. Instrumentations
      SHOULD set it to `true` only when they can reliably determine that context
      compaction was applied. Instrumentations SHOULD NOT set it to `false`; they
      SHOULD leave it unset otherwise.
```
@trask I like your suggestion. I used it. Thanks for the help.
